origin_model.before: cdn.EdgeURL = DELIVERY_CDN_BASE_URL + "/" + <storage object key>; the edge pulled from the object store
origin_model.after: cdn.EdgeURL = DELIVERY_CDN_BASE_URL + <this api's media route path and query> + the edge-origin marker; the edge pulls from the api
consequences: the media bucket needs no public read policy; every edge miss and revalidation re-runs the route's own authorization
the edge caches the API's Content-Type, Content-Disposition and Cache-Control
the ?v= generation tag reaches the edge as part of the cache key
purge names URLs, which is what an edge holds entries under
unchanged: presign (A32) remains the direct-to-bucket path when no CDN is configured
HLS playlists and storyboard.vtt are still never redirected — they are the generation switch
credentialed reads (?pt=, Authorization) stay on the proxy at private, no-store and are never rewritten to the edge

edge_detection.mechanism: a marker query parameter the api mints into every edge URL and reads back
edge_detection.why_not_a_trusted_header: it works, but forgetting to configure it at the CDN IS the redirect loop, and it makes the feature unusable on any edge that cannot add an origin header
edge_detection.why_not_the_host_header: some CDNs preserve the edge Host to the origin and some send the origin's own, so it is a signal that silently is not there on half the providers
edge_detection.why_this: the api puts the marker in the URL it mints, so the edge carries it to the origin as part of the request it was asked for — no operator configuration, nothing to forget, and it cannot loop
edge_detection.not_a_credential: anyone may send it; all it can do is decline the redirect and take the authoritative path, through the same authorization every media route already runs — which an unauthenticated caller can already force today with any Authorization header
edge_detection.second_property: because the marker is part of the URL, the edge's origin request and a viewer's request are DIFFERENT URLs, so the shared cache policy attaches to a URL only the edge ever asks for, with no Vary
edge_detection.operator_requirement: the CDN must forward the query string to the origin, which it must do anyway for ?v=

cache_headers.rule: shared = FromEdge AND Eligible AND NOT Credentialed

table.class: thumbnail / storyboard / avatar / banner / playlist cover

table.viewer_or_intermediary: private, no-store (was: no directive at all)

cache_headers.content_type_and_disposition: set by the api on the proxy path, so they reach the edge by construction; core #197's stored-object content type remains the presign-path fix

addressing_scheme.read: once per RUN (transcode.Service.runTarget), so a retry recomputes the same prefix

prefixes.hls: media.HLSPrefixForGeneration(videoID, n) -> streaming-playlists/<id> for 0, streaming-playlists/<id>/rN for N
prefixes.web_video: media.WebVideoPrefixForGeneration(videoID, n) -> web-videos/<id> for 0, web-videos/<id>/rN for N

addressing_scheme.one_scheme: rN keeps meaning generation directory — the shape source replacement already used and mediagc already parses. What changed is what advances N; a replacement still gets a fresh directory because it enqueues a transcode.
addressing_scheme.backfill: existing rows are set to their current source version, so the counter never re-issues a directory name a previous replacement used
addressing_scheme.url_effect: a new generation moves the master key, so hlsCacheVersion (updated_at derived) moves too — the new generation is a new KEY and a new ?v=, and therefore a new edge URL

old_generation_lifecycle.at_promotion: nothing is deleted; in-flight viewers keep working off the URLs they already hold
old_generation_lifecycle.collector: internal/mediagc, the orphan rule (A24). The HLS tree is collected at the generation level: the promoted generation (from streaming_playlists.master_key) and the TARGET generation are kept, everything else under streaming-playlists/<id>/ is orphan
old_generation_lifecycle.target_generation_source: videos.transcode_generation, not the source key's version — since 0136 those are different numbers, and the old inference would read "" for an in-flight same-source rerun and sweep a half-written tree
old_generation_lifecycle.web_videos: the same in-flight rule was added for web-videos/<id>/rN/, which had none: a generation's progressive MP4s are unreferenced between the first PUT and the promotion
old_generation_lifecycle.purge: none needed for a re-transcode — the new generation is a new URL, so no edge entry can answer for it

purge.unit: media route path with query (delivery.Resolver.Purge(ctx, mediaPath))
purge.why: one object is reachable at more than one route, and an edge holds entries under URLs
purge.more_precise_than_keys: closing downloads on a video used to purge the original's KEY, evicting /original as well as /download/original and cold-starting every viewer's progressive fallback to enforce a gate that does not apply to playback
purge.smaller_than_keys: the ladder's manifests left the set (an m3u8 is never redirected, so purging its key was always a wasted call), as did the download derivatives' raw keys, replaced by the /download routes the edge holds them under
purge.new_incompleteness_named: a superseded generation's children were served at today's paths under a DIFFERENT ?v=, which is not recorded once the playlist row moves on; their presence in the store is reported through the existing complete=false signal (log field renamed key_set_complete -> url_set_complete)
purge.known_gap_carried: a channel handle rename leaves the old /api/v1/channels/<old>/avatar at the edge under a name nothing can reconstruct
